hero_kpi_rationale: Operating cash flow is the key KPI for CoreCivic as it reflects the operational ability to generate liquidity from volatile government clients. With $194.6M in 2025 versus $269.2M in 2024, this metric captures the impact of policy changes (Trump executive orders) on federal contracts and demonstrates operational resilience despite government payment delays.

kpis.name: Operating Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash flow generated from operating activities
kpis.description: Cash flow generated from the company's operating activities. Down 27.6% compared to 2024 due to a $130.1M increase in working capital changes, partially offset by a $50.3M increase in facility net income.
kpis.signal: Declining cash flow due to working capital changes

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt composed of $238.5M in 4.75% Senior Notes, $500.0M in 8.25% Senior Notes, $134.3M in Kansas Notes, $112.5M in Term Loan, and $245.0M in Revolving Credit Facility. No debt maturities until October 2027.
kpis.signal: Diversified debt structure with staggered maturities

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Investment spending for activation and maintenance
kpis.description: Total capital expenditures of $140.6M in 2025, including $75.0M for activation of idle facilities and transportation vehicles, and $65.3M for facility development and maintenance. Expected reduction to $35-40M in 2026.
kpis.signal: Significant investment to activate 5 idle facilities and transportation services

kpis.name: Share Repurchase
kpis.description: Repurchased 11.2 million shares in 2025 at a total cost of $218.4M ($19.48 per share), excluding program fees. In total, 25.7 million shares have been repurchased for $399.5M ($15.52 per share). Remaining authorization of $300.5M.
kpis.signal: Capital return to shareholders via share repurchase

kpis.name: Cash on Hand
kpis.description: Cash balance of $97.9M as of December 31, 2025, supplemented by $311.4M available under the revolving credit facility. Sufficient capacity to cover planned capital expenditures and growth opportunities.
kpis.signal: Adequate liquidity with additional flexibility via credit facility

kpis.name: Operating Facilities
kpis.description: 44 correctional and detention facilities (40 owned or controlled under long-term leases) with total capacity of 68,000 beds. Plus 20 residential reentry centers (4,000 beds) and 5 properties in the Properties segment (8,000 beds potential).
kpis.signal: Extensive network with 68,000-bed capacity plus Community and Properties segments

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Revenue of $2.211B in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of $0.122B in the latest fiscal year (FY2022).

risks.title: Political changes affecting government contracts
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions President Trump's executive orders of January 20, 2025, and the Laken Riley Act, which directly increase demand for ICE detention services (58.2% increase noted). However, this also creates future volatility if administrations change. The intensity of language around immigration policy is high and central to operations.

risks.title: Dependence on federal government contracts
risks.score_rationale: The company is significantly dependent on three federal agencies: ICE (DHS), BOP, and USMS (DOJ). Loss or reduction of contracts with these agencies would represent a major revenue risk. Current payment delays post-shutdown confirm this.

risks.title: Government payment delays and budget shutdowns
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly states: 'We continue to experience payment delays from our federal customers following the most recent government shutdown' and 'due to newly added approval requirements of certain invoices by DHS'. This directly impacts operating cash flows.

risks.title: ICE demand volatility
risks.score_rationale: Although ICE demand increased by 58.2% following Trump's executive orders, history shows prior termination of the Dilley contract. This volatility makes capacity planning and investment decisions complex and risky.

risks.title: Idle capacity and activation costs
risks.score_rationale: The company maintains several idle facilities. The $75.0M investment in 2025 aims to activate 5 facilities. If anticipated demand does not materialize, these facilities would remain costly liabilities. Planned capex reductions to $35-40M in 2026 indicate caution.

risks.title: Risk of contract termination for convenience
risks.score_rationale: Standard documentation indicates that management contracts 'generally provide customers with the right to terminate our contracts at any time without cause'. While standard in the industry, this creates fundamental uncertainty regarding revenue sustainability.

risks.title: Litigation over permits and approvals
risks.score_rationale: Although mentioned in underlying risk analysis, the provided 10-K does not detail current specific litigation regarding permits. However, historically, facilities such as Leavenworth and California City have experienced permit-related delays.

ai_positioning.summary: CoreCivic does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/8-K disclosures. The information provided focuses on detention and reentry operations, government contracts, and the impacts of policy changes.
